Theme

Town, shops & places · Money, work & business

price noun

also ask the price, charge, fee, what do you charge?, charge a price for, set a price, fix a price, at a high price, at a low price, higher price

classical

Traupman 364

pretium, pretiī n.

noun, second declension

Other words

  • mercēs, mercēdis f. — fee, charge (for work or a service); wages, rent

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.126: quī cum mercēde docēret; Phaedr. 1.8.12: et mercēdem postulēs

    What is paid for work or for the use of something, as pretium is what goods cost.

  • indicō, indicāre, indicāvī, indicātum — name a price, ask so much: charge

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Pers. 586: Indicā, fac pretium.; M-O s.v. sale: ask (a certain price) for something, charge

    With the genitive of price: quantī indicās?, how much are you asking? (Vives, cited by Morgan–Owens). Not to be confused with indīcō, indīcere, to proclaim.

  • pretium facere — set a price (of a seller or a buyer)

    also used · classical · Plaut. Pers. 4.4.37: indicā, fac pretium (Lewis & Short); Traupman 376

  • pretium statuere — set, fix a price

    also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 3.1.133: pretium statuere mercī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 376

Examples

  • mercis pretium inquīrere

    ask the priceTraupman 130–131

  • Indicā, fac pretium. — Tua mers est, tua indicātiōst.

    Name your price. — They’re your goods; the pricing is yours.Plaut. Pers. 586

  • pretium cōnstituere (+ dat.)

    to charge a price for, set a price onTraupman 289

  • magnō (parvō, minimō, nimiō)

    at a high (low, very low, exorbitant) priceTraupman 364

  • pretium amplius

    a higher priceTraupman 364

  • pretium facere

    to set a priceTraupman 364

  • Pretium eī in lībrās est decem dēnāriīs.

    The price for it is ten denarii a pound.Traupman 364

See also how much is it?, set a price, cost a lot, cheap, expensive.
